source.section: Alone, Together: A Model of Social (Mis)Learning from Consumer Reviews
source.quote: History: Anthony Dukes served as the senior editor.
This paper studies the nature and impact of consumer reviews in horizontally differentiated product markets.

This is because high-quality products end up inducing purchases (and, thus, reviews) even by buyers for whom the fit compo­ nent of consumer satisfaction1 is relatively lower (the curse of the best seller).

However, the key observation is that these biases are highly product-specific: for some product characteristics (which we characterize in our main propositions), we observe a drastic increase in average reviews and de­ crease in variance; for others, both changes are much smaller.

source.quote: Learning from reviews, however, is made difficult by the fact that, to some extent, reviews measure idiosyncratic consumer–product fit and not just objective quality.
